description: Rhizoctonia root rot and damping-off is a common soilborne fungal disease that attacks seeds, seedlings, and plant roots. It causes stem lesions near the soil line, root rot, and the collapse of young plants.
symptoms: Seedlings collapsing at the soil line
Brown or reddish lesions on stems near the soil surface
Root rot and poor root development
Irregular patches of dead or weak plants in the field
visual_symptoms: brown sunken lesions at soil line
spread: Movement of soil on tools or machinery
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil and plant debris
It infects seeds or young seedlings
Lesions develop on stems and roots
The pathogen spreads through soil contact
cultural_control: Avoid planting in cold or very wet soil
biological_control: Use beneficial fungi such as Trichoderma species
Use beneficial bacteria like Bacillus subtilis
